clusters.name: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction

standards.skillName: One- and Two-Step Word Problems within 100
standards.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing situations, with unknowns in all positions.
standards.ccssText: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

standards.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies; by end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.
standards.ccssText: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.

clusters.name: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication

standards.description: Determine whether a group of objects has an odd or even number of members; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.
standards.ccssText: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

standards.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.
standards.ccssText: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

domains.name: Number and Operations in Base Ten

standards.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones.
standards.ccssText: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones.

subStandards.description: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a "hundred."
The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

standards.description: Count within 1000 and skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s.
standards.ccssText: Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s.

standards.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
standards.ccssText: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

standards.description: Compare two three-digit numbers based on the values of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols.
standards.ccssText: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

clusters.name: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract

standards.description: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
standards.ccssText: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

standards.skillName: Adding up to Four Two-Digit Numbers
standards.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using place value strategies and properties of operations.
standards.ccssText: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

standards.description: Add and subtract within 1000 using place value strategies, composing and decomposing tens and hundreds as needed.
standards.ccssText: Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

standards.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to any number from 100 to 900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from any number from 100 to 900.
standards.ccssText: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100–900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100–900.

standards.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value understanding and properties of operations.
standards.ccssText: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.

clusters.name: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units

standards.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.
standards.ccssText: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

standards.description: Measure the length of an object twice using two different length units and describe how the measurements relate to the size of the unit.
standards.ccssText: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

standards.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
standards.ccssText: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

standards.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the difference in terms of a standard length unit.
standards.ccssText: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

clusters.name: Relate addition and subtraction to length

standards.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths given in the same units.
standards.ccssText: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

standards.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths on a number line and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line.
standards.ccssText: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, ..., and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

standards.skillName: Telling Time to the Nearest Five Minutes
standards.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.
standards.ccssText: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

standards.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using dollar and cent symbols appropriately.
standards.ccssText: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately. Example: If you have 2 dimes and 3 pennies, how many cents do you have?

standards.description: Generate measurement data and show measurements on a line plot with a whole-number scale.
standards.ccssText: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.

standards.description: Draw picture graphs and bar graphs to represent data with up to four categories and solve simple comparison problems using the graphs.
standards.ccssText: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.

clusters.name: Reason with shapes and their attributes

standards.description: Recognize and draw shapes with specified attributes such as number of angles or equal faces; identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.
standards.ccssText: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.

standards.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number.
standards.ccssText: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

standards.skillName: Equal Shares: Halves, Thirds, and Fourths
standards.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares and describe them using words like halves, thirds, and fourths.
standards.ccssText: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
